title: AxonFlow typed policy authoring document
description: The versioned typed authoring document of ADR-065. It is the source of truth for policy: generated Rego is never the source, and this document is what an authoring API accepts, renders back without loss, compiles into a signed bundle, and diffs. Every enum below is held to the Go declarations by a test, so a value the compiler understands and this schema does not is a build failure rather than a portal that silently refuses a valid policy.

api_version.description: The version of the authoring envelope. Distinct from the decision contract version and from the author's own revision number.

document_id.description: Stable identity across versions. A version bump changes policy.version and never this.

author.description: The principal that saved this version. It is inside the signed source because separation of duties at publication is checked against it.

supersedes.description: The artifact digest this version was edited from. A digest rather than a version number, so that two authors who both start from version 4 agree on the number and disagree on the parent.

identifier.description: A canonical identifier. Display names, emails, token claims, connector names and aliases are never identifiers.

qualifier.description: The realm or connector identifier. Present for qualified kinds and empty for the rest.

version.description: The author's revision number. Promotion advances it; rollback is the operation that does not.

attributes.description: Every policy-visible attribute this document may reference. A condition over a path absent from this list is refused at save time.

interactive_realms.description: Whether a person can be asked a question in each realm, carried so a signed bundle is self contained. It is DERIVED from the registry by the authoring constructor and refused when it disagrees, so it is never a second source of truth.

root.description: The signing authority. System and organization roots are separate signed artifacts verified against different keys, so an organization permission cannot modify a system constraint.

optional.description: Whether authoritative absence is possible. It permits, but does not by itself decide, a non-match on absence: the policy must also say what absence means.

max_age_seconds.description: The freshness bound. A value outside it becomes unknown rather than stale-but-usable. Zero means unbounded.

unless.description: An exception clause. A satisfied exception collapses the policy to non-applicable, which is the same code path as the policy not existing.

pierceable_by.description: The break-glass roles that may suspend this control. Absent means unbreakable by construction, which is what a regulatory or contractual constraint declares.

authority.description: What a policy is allowed to do, not where it executes. A permission only widens, a constraint only restricts, a requirement attaches a mandatory obligation, and an inspection policy cannot grant.

required_tags.description: Conjunctive: the action must carry every tag. A constraint over the pair of irreversible and pii_egress expresses something no combination of single-tag constraints reaches.

any.description: Selects every registered action. It must be set explicitly, so that an empty selector is a construction defect rather than an accidental match-all.

condition.description: One node of the typed condition tree. There is no raw Rego anywhere in this document: the compiler owns condition generation, which is what makes the tri-state guarantees enforceable.

absence_handling.description: What a condition does when the authoritative source established that its attribute has no value. It is required on a condition over an optional attribute and forbidden otherwise, and caller-supplied absence is always unknown.

target.description: The canonical field path for a disclosure transform. Empty for every other family.

mandatory.description: A mandatory obligation denies when it cannot be discharged. An advisory one is recorded and dropped.
